title: Feminine grammatical forms attached to the extended-prenomen titulary
sources: Bezel UC 1927 Ankhetkheperure (Samson, COA III 230); pectoral Carter 261p(1) ankh(t)-kheperure mer(yt)-Waenre + maat-kheru (Gabolde 2009 p. 116-117; Eaton-Krauss OLZ 98, 2003, 47); coffinette 266g Selkis line 7 akhet-en-hies (Gabolde 2009 p. 117); bracelets (Sousa et al. 2024); UC 410, NRP plaster, Munich AeS 7342 akhet-en-hies (Dietrich 2024 p. 101-102). Counter: Kemp 2016 p. 18-20, 28-29 (t may be r or n on bezels; .ti endings are second person).

title: The nomen Neferneferuaten is Nefertiti's own cartouche name (Neferneferuaten-Nefertiti from about year 5), written with the same reversed Aten group
sources: Harris 1973 AcOr 35; Kemp 2016 p. 22 (reversed Aten group noted, explained as scribal habit); Allen 2009 p. 12 on the daughter Neferneferuaten-tasherit.

title: Epithets tying the ruler to Akhenaten as his beloved and to a husband: mery-Waenre, mery-Neferkheperure, akhet-en-hies 'effective for her husband'
sources: Gabolde 1998 p. 153-157 (reading accepted by Murnane 2001, Eaton-Krauss & Krauss 2001, Hornung 2006, Dodson 2009); Kemp 2016 p. 22 reads the husband as Ankhkheperure himself; Krauss 2007 gives the epithet to a widow of Ankhkheperure.

title: Stela UC 410 + Cairo JE 64959: the double cartouche of Neferneferuaten is cut over Nefertiti's single queenly cartouche and a king's-daughter caption
sources: Allen JARCE 25 (1988) via Allen 2009 n. 5, 12; Krauss BSEG 13 (1989); Gabolde BSEG 14 (1990); COA III 231-233 (Samson, Fairman); Kemp 2016 p. 23-26 with Gabolde's tracing; Dietrich 2024 p. 102.

title: Paired-ruler scenes: an adult woman in the blue crown beside a male king, both with uraeus, interacting as living rulers; the Hermopolis pillar join names Neferneferuaten and King's Daughter Ankhesenpaaten
sources: Berlin AeM 17813 and 20716 (Harris 1973; Allen 2009 figs 3-4; Dietrich 2024 p. 98); Ranefer sealing COA I pl. X.6; Hermopolis 406/VII + 777/VIII (Johnson 2020, as reported by Dietrich 2024 p. 102-104) + 826/VIIIA (Gabolde 1990; Dietrich fig. 3). Counter: Harris 1973 read the figures as king and crowned queen; Kemp 2016 p. 15 doubts coregency.

title: Box Carter 1k: Akhenaten 'great in his lifetime', then Ankhkheperure-mery-Neferkheperure Neferneferuaten-mery-Waenre, then King's Great Wife Meritaten 'may she live', as three entries in one protocol
sources: Carter cards 001k-1..4; Newberry JEA 14 (1928) 4-5; Dietrich 2024 p. 100-101; Allen 2009 p. 9-10 and n. 6; Kemp 2016 p. 13-15 (reads the box as posthumous respect to Akhenaten and as proof the king was married to Meritaten); Gabolde 1998 p. 178-179 reads Meritaten in apposition to Neferneferuaten (rejected by Murnane 2001, Eaton-Krauss & Krauss 2001, Allen 2009, Dodson 2020, Kemp 2016).

title: Tomb of Meryre II (Amarna tomb 2) and the Memphis block: King Ankhkheperure Smenkhkare Djeserkheperu with King's Great Wife Meritaten, under the Aten, in a tomb whose dated decoration ends with the year-12 durbar
sources: Davies 1905 pl. XLI after Lepsius LD III 99a; Petrie 1894 p. 29; Newberry JEA 14 (1928) 5-6 (Memphis); Kemp 2016 p. 15 (year 12 dates the event, not the carving); Allen 2009 p. 9 and 17; Dodson 2020 p. 68-71.

title: Calcite jar Carter 405: Akhenaten's cartouches followed by Smenkhkare's, both later erased; the only object joining the two names
sources: Carter cards 405-1/2; Loeben, Amarna Letters 3 (1994) as cited; Allen 2009 p. 9 fig. 1; Dietrich 2024 p. 102 ('at best circumstantial' for a coregency).

title: Complementary distribution of the names: the plain prenomen only with the nomen Smenkhkare, the extended prenomen only with the nomen Neferneferuaten, with no crossed example among hundreds of bezels and moulds
sources: Allen JARCE 25 (1988) 126; Allen 1991: 84-85; Gabolde 1998: 153-157; Harris 1992: 60-61 (all as cited by Dietrich 2024 p. 101); Petrie 1894 pl. XV; COA III bezel lists.

title: Pairi graffito TT 139: 'Year 3, III Akhet 10' of Ankhkheperure-mery-[...] Neferneferuaten-mery-[...], with Amun worshipped and a 'House of Ankhkheperure in Thebes' staffed by priests of Amun; Smenkhkare is otherwise attested only in Aten contexts
sources: Gardiner JEA 14 (1928) 10-11 pls V-VI; Newberry JEA 14, 3-9; Krauss in Hornung-Krauss-Warburton 2006 p. 207-208; Dodson 2020b (Fs Hawass) and Reeves 2023 (Fs Strudwick) as reported by Dietrich 2024 n. 15, 18; Dietrich n. 18 on the two theologies.

title: Amarna jar dockets: Akhenaten's highest year 17; a year-17 docket relabelled 'year 1' (COA III 279); years 1-3 of a successor at Amarna; 'House of Smenkhkare, [justified]' in a year 1 (no. 35); 'House of Ankhkheperure' as a separate estate (no. 36)
sources: Petrie 1894 p. 32-34 (Griffith); COA III (Fairman) p. 143-159, 199; Krauss 2006 p. 207-208; Allen 2009 p. 12 and n. 14; Dodson 2009 p. 31 n. 14.

title: Manetho according to Josephus: Orus, then 'his daughter Akencheres, 12 years 1 month', then 'her brother Rathotis, 9 years'
sources: Josephus, Contra Apionem 1.96-97 (Niese); Waddell 1940 fr. 50-53; Krauss 1978 p. 43-53 and Hornung-Krauss-Warburton 2006 p. 36, 207; Allen 2009 p. 18; Dodson 2020 p. 104-105, 128; Kemp 2016 p. 30 ('nothing is gained').

title: A shabti of Nefertiti with queenly titles only (Louvre AF 9904 + Brooklyn 33.51)
sources: Loeben MDAIK 42 (1986) 99-107 and EAO 13 (1999); Bovot EAO 13 (1999) 31-34 (two shabtis); Allen 2009 p. 16 n. 59; Dodson 2020 p. 89 (made in anticipation of death); Reeves 2015 n. 35.

title: Masculine references beside the extended names: 'my lord' with a masculine article on Ranefer's door jamb; the North Riverside Palace prenomen painted with r, not t, under mer
sources: Kemp 2016 p. 13, 20-21 (with Weatherhead's and Hilda Pendlebury's copies); Kemp & Stevens 2010 p. 119-127 (not seen).

title: Age of Neferneferuaten-tasherit: fourth daughter, shown as a child at the year-12 durbar, so at most about ten years old in year 17
sources: Davies 1905 pl. XXXVIII (six daughters); Allen 2009 p. 15-16; Dodson 2020 p. 129 on Allen's withdrawal.

title: Dayr Abu Hinnis graffito: Nefertiti still King's Great Wife on day 15 of a month of Akhet in year 16, about a year before Akhenaten's death
sources: Van der Perre 2012; 2014 JEgH 7, 67-108 (abstract only); Dodson 2020 p. 72-73 fig. 80; Reeves 2015 n. 32.

title: A full kingly burial outfit made for the female king was left unused and re-inscribed for Tutankhamun (coffinettes, pectoral, trappings, middle coffin, mask, second shrine, statuettes)
sources: Gabolde 2009 p. 116-118; Reeves 2015 JAEI 7.4 and ARTP OP1; Laboury 2002; Engelbach ASAE 40 (1940); Sousa-Pieke-Bagh 2024 (Broschat); Kemp 2016 p. 26-29 (shrine endings read as second person).

title: Two rulers with one prenomen: Ankhkheperure is shared by the Smenkhkare name-set and the Neferneferuaten name-set, which has no parallel for two successive kings
sources: Harris 1973 AcOr 35 p. 5-13 (the one-person argument); Reeves 2015 ARTP OP1 n. 33; Kemp 2016 p. 15; Allen 2009 p. 12-13 and Dodson 2020 p. 79 (continuity explanations for two persons).

title: Age at death of the KV55 body: six hands-on examiners give 19-26; Harris and Wente 30-35 and Hawass 2010 (CT, criteria unpublished) 35-45; Akhenaten had a daughter by about year 2 and reigned 17 years
sources: Elliot Smith 1912; Derry ASAE 31 (1931); Harrison JEA 52 (1966); Filer 2000; Strouhal 2010; Duhig 2010; Hawass et al. JAMA 303 (2010); Gabolde 2009 p. 12 (26-27 for Akhenaten); dossier B section 2.

title: Inscribed material in KV55: magic bricks of Akhenaten, Kiya's coffin re-worked with Akhenaten's epithets (cartouches later cut out), Kiya's canopic jars, Tiye's shrine, sealings of Tutankhamun; no name of Smenkhkare
sources: Davis 1910; Allen 2009 n. 24-26; Gabolde 2009 p. 3-6, 12-18; Dodson 2009 ch. 2 and 2020 p. 47-48; Reeves 2001 p. 81-84; dossier B section 1.

title: 2010 STR pedigree (8 loci): KV55 a son of Amenhotep III and KV35EL (Tiye) and the father of Tutankhamun with KV35YL; no independent replication; Gad et al. 2020 same team
sources: Hawass et al. JAMA 303 (2010) 638-647; Gad et al. 2020; Lorenzen & Willerslev JAMA 2010; Marchant Nature 2011; Phizackerley 2010 (D7S820); Gabolde ENiM 6 (2013); dossier B sections 3-4.

title: Tutankhaten was 'King's Son of his body' at Amarna; if the pedigree holds, his father is the KV55 man, who must therefore have been a king
sources: Hermopolis talatat 56-VIIIA + 831-VIIIC (Allen 2009 fig. 5, p. 14-17; Dodson 2014 fig. 104).

title: The name: Ni-ip-hu-ru-ri-ia-as (KBo 14.12 iv 18) against Nebkheperure (Tutankhamun) and Neferkheperure (Akhenaten); EA 9 addressed to Nibhurrereya
sources: Güterbock JCS 10 (1956) 94-98; Miller AoF 34 (2007) 252-293 (EA 9 = Akhenaten); Bryce 1990; Federn JCS 14 (1960) 33; dossier C section 2.4.

title: The Armaa synchronism: Horemheb acts in Syria as a non-king in years 7-9 of Mursili II (KUB 19.15 + KBo 50.24), which sits badly with a Nibhururiya who died only four years before Horemheb's accession
sources: Miller 2007; Devecchi & Miller 2011; contra Stempel GM 213 (2007) and Theis 2011 as cited by Dodson 2020 n. 44; Bryce 1990, Klinger 2006, Freu 2004 for Tutankhamun; dossier C sections 5-6.

title: Season: the death message reached Suppiluliuma during the Carchemish campaign (late summer or autumn) and Hani came back in spring; Tutankhamun's burial flowers point to a death in winter; Akhenaten died after the year-17 vintage
sources: Deeds fragment 28 (Güterbock 1956 p. 94-98); floral evidence of KV62 (Hepper 1990) as used by Belmonte 2013; Fairman COA III 157-159 on docket 279; dossier C section 7.

title: The widow's plea: 'my husband died, a son I have not, I will never take a servant of mine and make him my husband'; Ankhesenamun was later paired with Ay on a ring; Nefertiti and Meritaten each had daughters and a boy in the family
sources: Deeds fragment 28 A iii 7-15 (Güterbock 1956); Newberry JEA 18 (1932) 50 (Ay-Ankhesenamun ring); Reeves 2001 ch. 9; Allen 2009 n. 62.

title: Lupakki's raid on Amka at the time of the king's death (Deeds) matches EA 170 from the Amarna archive, and the envoy Hani of the Deeds appears in EA 161, 162 and 369
sources: EA 170 and 161-162, 369 (Knudtzon 1915; Moran 1992 as cited); Deeds fragment 28; Miller 2007; Reeves 2001 p. 176-177; dossier C section 6.

title: Hittite relative chronology: the plague prayers, the 20-year plague, and the solar omen of Mursili's year 10 (eclipse of 24 June 1312 if that is the omen)
sources: CTH 378.2 (Rieken's score); KUB 14.4 (omen); Belmonte 2013 p. 427-429; Dodson 2020 chronology table; dossier C section 7.

title: Consistency of the plea with the Egyptian succession: a widow writes that Egypt has no king; a coregent already on the throne, or an Egyptian king who acceded after months of negotiation for a Hittite prince, fit that less well
sources: Deeds fragment 28; Reeves 2001 ch. 9 (Nefertiti seeking a consort); Allen 2009 n. 62 (no demotion implied); Gabolde 1998 p. 213-226 (Zannanza = Smenkhkare), judged 'not probable' by Hornung-Krauss-Warburton 2006 n. 73.

title: 'A son he has not' against Tutankhaten's existence: if the dead king was Tutankhaten's father, the statement is false for the royal house
sources: Deeds fragment 28 A iii 7-15 and E3 iv 1-39 (Hani's speech); Hermopolis King's Son block; JAMA 2010 pedigree.
